briefs.rationale: Skolem's construction is the incidence-structure export of the same counting discipline the part already teaches. The rewrite keeps the sum-rule, product-rule, factorial, binomial, inclusion-exclusion and pigeonhole development, condenses the additive-character orthogonality interface to $1$ on equal characters and $0$ otherwise with nontrivial characters summing to zero (proved from representation orthogonality, with the choice-free dictionary to one-dimensional complex representations), and closes the arc with the gained page: two-designs and Steiner systems, and the explicit block families of Skolem's Steiner triple system of order $6m+1$ from a half-idempotent quasigroup, each pair of points covered exactly once. This keeps the brief inside the 120-word budget.

The seven gained pages extend the part's contour-to-Riemann-surface arc. Bergman and Szegő kernels add the reproducing-kernel and invariant-metric side of the Hardy theory; Hodge decomposition, divisors, Riemann-Roch and Abel-Jacobi theory turn periods and Jacobians of compact surfaces into global invariants; extremal length, quasiconformality, the Beltrami equation with its measurable Riemann mapping theorem, and quasisymmetric welding with conformal removability carry the conformal side past the Riemann mapping theorem. The original chain (Goursat-Cauchy, Poisson-Dirichlet-Green-capacity, Fatou-Blaschke, Hartogs-pseudoconvexity-Hörmander, Runge-Mittag-Leffler, Poisson-Jensen, Montel-Schwarz-Pick-Bloch-Schottky-Picard, monodromy, uniformization, elliptic and modular functions, zeta) is condensed into thematic roles so the brief stays within the 120-word budget.

The old brief was a placeholder that named no page. The rewrite states the part's arc: finite-group methods from characters and induced characters through Brauer's modular theory to blocks, defect groups and the Green correspondence; the modular function and $L^1$ group algebras opening the analytic half; unitary representations, positive type and GNS, compact-group complete reducibility and Peter-Weyl, induced representations and Mackey imprimitivity, group C*-algebras and the Fell dual; then the gained pages — amenability through Reiter nets and Følner sets, direct integral decomposition into factor and type-I representations, and Kazhdan's property (T) with its spectral gap — closed by the two SL2(R) pages computing the principal, complementary and discrete series and the irreducible unitary dual. The pathway-sync insertion had folded the gained page lines into the part slug; this rewrite moves them into the part's pages list, restoring the stable slug representation-theory and the page order.

The rewrite covers the symmetric-group arc — partitions, tableaux and permutation modules; Specht modules; branching and the hook-length formula with Robinson-Schensted; symmetric functions with the Hall inner product and Schur bases; the Frobenius characteristic; Jucys-Murphy elements and seminormal forms; integral Specht modules and their modular simples; Plancherel measure and asymptotic Young diagrams — and integrates the three gained pages as its continuation: outer products, skew Specht modules and Littlewood-Richardson coefficients for induction and restriction; Kazhdan-Lusztig bases, polynomials and cells carrying the combinatorics into Hecke algebras; quantized enveloping algebras and quantum Serre relations opening the quantum-group track. The stale sentence calling the asymptotic page a draft is dropped because that page is published; the pathway-sync insertion is moved out of the mangled part slug into the part's pages list.

The gained page belongs to this part by the sync's placement, so the rewrite keeps the locally finite refinement and partition-of-unity material, the Tychonoff embedding and Stone-Cech compactification, and the uniformity account of completeness, and closes with the metric-space construction: assuming choice, separated closed cores produce discrete open families at each scale whose countable union is a sigma-discrete basis, with the exact conventions the metrization criteria use. The earlier wording is otherwise preserved and condensed only where the gained material required it.
